title: The Imperative with a Definite Object

sections.title: The same choice you already make
sections.content: You already choose between definite and indefinite conjugation depending on the object — eszem levest ("I eat soup", general) vs. eszem a levest ("I eat the soup", a specific one). The imperative makes exactly the same choice: a command with a definite object ("the onion", not just "some onion") uses the DEFINITE imperative ending instead of -j.

sections.title: Indefinite vs. definite command
rows: Put the salt in the soup! (this salt)

items.english: Put the meat in the pot!

sections.content: süt ("to bake, fry") and tesz ("to put") are irregular here — süsd and tedd don't just add an ending, the stem itself changes shape. Treat süsd and tedd as forms worth memorizing whole, the same way you already memorized menj.
